## Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Languages

::: {.key-question}
What proportion of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in the NEPHU catchment speak an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander language at home?
:::

::: {.ctg-box}
**This topic aligns with [Closing the Gap Outcome Area 16](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/culture-and-languages/): Cultures and languages are strong, supported and flourishing**

Target: By 2031, there is a sustained increase in number and strength of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander languages being spoken.
:::

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Aboriginal language spoken at home, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
language_any_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Language_LGA.csv",
                                      variable = "language_home") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(language_home != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
language_any_lga <- language_any_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(language_home = dplyr::case_when(
    language_home == "Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Language used at home" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = language_home,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Aboriginal language spoken at home, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
language_any_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Language_AgeSex.csv",
                                            variable = "language_home") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(language_home != "Not stated")

# Data wrangling
language_any_agesex <- language_any_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(language_home = dplyr::case_when(
    language_home == "Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Language used at home" ~ "yes",
    TRUE ~ "no")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = language_home,
                          dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander languages
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
language_specific <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Language_Specific.csv",
                                       variable = "language")

# Data wrangling
language_specific <- language_specific %>%
  dplyr::filter(lga_name %in% c(nephu_lga)) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(language = dplyr::case_when(
    language == "Australian Indigenous Languages, nfd"       ~ "Australian Indigenous Languages",
    language == "Other Australian Indigenous Languages, nec" ~ "Australian Indigenous Languages",
    language == "Aboriginal English, so described"           ~ "Aboriginal English",
    language == "Torres Strait Island Languages, nfd"        ~ "Torres Strait Island Languages",
    TRUE ~ as.character(language))) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_n = aboriginal + torres_strait_islander + both_aboriginal_and_torres_strait_islander) %>%
  #
  dplyr::group_by(language) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(aboriginal_n = sum(aboriginal_n)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(aboriginal_n > 0) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(desc(aboriginal_n), language) %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_prop = aboriginal_n / population_nephu_aboriginal * 100)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 2.1% (n = 250) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census reported speaking an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander language at home.

- The number of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who reported speaking an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander language at home ranged from 62 (Darebin LGA) to 0 (Nillumbik LGA). 

- The percentage of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who reported speaking an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander language at home ranged from 7.6% (Yarra LGA) to 0.0% (Nillumbik LGA). 

- Younger people (aged < 50 years) were more likely to report speaking an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander language, with no speakers aged > 60 years reported in the NEPHU catchment. There were a higher number of female speakers than male speakers across most age groups (except 40-49 years). 

- Data on which languages were spoken were available for 181 people. The most common languages spoken at home by people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander were Australian Indigenous Languages (including those not further described or not elsewhere classified) (n = 73), Yorta Yorta (n = 27), Nyungar (n = 15), and Aboriginal English (n = 11).

- Further historical and ongoing target context can be found on the [Closing the Gap Information Repository](https://www.pc.gov.au/closing-the-gap-data/dashboard/outcome-area/culture-and-languages/).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- As discussed in stakeholder consultations during the development of this report, these data may not be a true indicator of Closing the Gap Target 16, as there may be an increase in people who are learning and speaking Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander languages but not necessarily speaking their language at home. 

- It was also discussed that higher engagement amongst young people and children may be partly due to the success of community-driven language teaching efforts. The [Victorian Aboriginal Corporation for Languages (VACL)](https://vacl.org.au/) assists local communities with language revitalisation plans by running language camps, school programs, and events. For example, they have [partnered with Thornbury Primary School since 2012](https://www.vaeai.org.au/6895/), where students from Prep to Grade 6 have been learning Woiwurrung, the language of the Wurundjeri People.

- The Fourth [National Indigenous Languages Surveys (NILS)](https://aiatsis.gov.au/research/languages/national-indigenous-languages-surveys) is currently underway, with data collection completed in February 2026. This survey has been co-designed with over 150 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander language representatives across Australia, from every state and territory.

::: {.callout-tip title="Census questions and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- The following question was asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021:
  - Does the person use a language other than English at home?
    - No, English only
    - Yes, Mandarin
    - Yes, Arabic
    - Yes, Cantonese
    - Yes, Vietnamese
    - Yes, Italian
    - Yes, Greek
    - Yes, other language (please specify)

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Definitions and notes:
  - `r note_aboriginality_census`
  - When a person listed more than one language, responses were accepted in the order they appeared on the Census form. The first response was included in the data and any extra responses were rejected. This may lead to underreporting of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander languages, as these responses were recorded as 'Yes, other languages (please specify)' and would not be included for people who also selected another language higher up on the list.

:::

## Other Languages

::: {.key-question}
What proportion of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in the NEPHU catchment use other languages at home?
:::

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Other languages
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
language_other <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Language_Other.csv",
                                    variable = "language")

# Data wrangling
language_other <- language_other %>%
  dplyr::filter(lga_name %in% c(nephu_lga)) %>%
  #
  dplyr::filter(!language %in% c("English", "Not stated", "Inadequately described", "Non-verbal, so described")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_n = aboriginal + torres_strait_islander + both_aboriginal_and_torres_strait_islander) %>%
  #
  dplyr::group_by(language) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(aboriginal_n = sum(aboriginal_n)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(aboriginal_n > 0) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(desc(aboriginal_n), language) %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_prop = aboriginal_n / population_nephu_aboriginal * 100)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 2.1% (n = 248) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census reported using a language other than English or other than an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander language at home. 

- The most common languages spoken at home by people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander were Italian (n = 38), Mandarin (n = 38), Arabic (n = 20), Greek (n = 19), and Spanish (n = 19). 

- 27 people reporting using Auslan at home.

::: {.callout-tip title="Census questions and definitions for this topic " icon=false collapse=false}
- The following question was asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021:
  - Does the person use a language other than English at home?
    - No, English only
    - Yes, Mandarin
    - Yes, Arabic
    - Yes, Cantonese
    - Yes, Vietnamese
    - Yes, Italian
    - Yes, Greek
    - Yes, other language (please specify)

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Definitions and notes:
  - `r note_aboriginality_census`
  - When a person listed more than one language, responses were accepted in the order they appeared on the Census form. The first response was included in the data and any extra responses were rejected. This may lead to underreporting of languages that are not explicitly listed in the question, as these responses were recorded as 'Yes, other languages (please specify)' and would not be included for people who also selected another language higher up on the list.

:::

## English Proficiency

::: {.key-question}
What is the average level of English proficiency for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in the NEPHU catchment?
:::

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# English proficiency, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
english_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_English_LGA.csv",
                                 variable = "english_proficiency") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_detect(english_proficiency, "Not stated"))

# Data wrangling
english_lga <- english_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(english_proficiency = dplyr::case_when(
    english_proficiency == "Uses other language and speaks English: Not well"   ~ "no",
    english_proficiency == "Uses other language and speaks English: Not at all" ~ "no",
    TRUE ~ "yes")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = english_proficiency,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "yes")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# English proficiency, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
english_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_English_AgeSex.csv",
                                       variable = "english_proficiency") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_detect(english_proficiency, "Not stated"))

# Data wrangling
english_agesex <- english_agesex %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(english_proficiency = dplyr::case_when(
    english_proficiency == "Uses other language and speaks English: Not well"   ~ "no",
    english_proficiency == "Uses other language and speaks English: Not at all" ~ "no",
    TRUE ~ "yes")) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = english_proficiency,
                          dichot   = "yes")
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Almost all people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander had a high level of English proficiency.

- This pattern was seen across all LGAs, for both males and females, and across all age groups.

::: {.callout-tip title="Census questions and definitions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- The following questions were asked of all people completing the ABS Census 2021:
  - Does the person use a language other than English at home?
    - No, English only
    - Yes, Mandarin
    - Yes, Arabic
    - Yes, Cantonese
    - Yes, Vietnamese
    - Yes, Italian
    - Yes, Greek
    - Yes, other language (please specify)
  - How well does the person speak English?
    - `r note_response_likert_verywell`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Definitions and notes:
  - `r note_aboriginality_census`
  - When a person listed more than one language, responses were accepted in the order they appeared on the Census form. The first response was included in the data and any extra responses were rejected. This may lead to underreporting of languages that are not explicitly listed in the question, as these responses were recorded as 'Yes, other languages (please specify)' and would not be included for people who also selected another language higher up on the list.

:::

```{r}
  write.csv(table, paste0(here::here(), "/data/", figtab_table_number, ".csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  
}

table %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_prop = sprintf("%.1f", aboriginal_prop)) %>% 
  #
  f_table_simple(column_width  = "2in",
                 table_headers = c("LGA",
                                   "Number of people",
                                   "Percent of people"))
```
